inquiries.question: Compact tombstones in #12, or ship #12 and compact them in a follow-up?
inquiries.context:
azulus asked on #12 why tombstones never go away: every sync ships the whole list, and on a long-lived notebook it only grows. They're right. Nothing in #12 or on main prunes it; `syncTombstones()` in src/sync/merge.ts:88 sends it whole on every pull.

Compacting is safe once every device has synced past a tombstone. The server already keeps each device's last full sync (`devices.last_full_sync`), so merge() can drop the ones older than the oldest of those. It's about 40 lines and a test.

priya wants #12 before Thursday's mobile freeze. #12 is green, and kai approved it before azulus's comment. I'd do it in #12: it's small, and shipping the growth to every phone first means a second migration later.

options.next: I add the pruning and a test that a week-old delete doesn't come back, push, and ask azulus and kai to look again. A day, likely before Thursday.
I reply to azulus that a follow-up does it, and open that PR today. #12 can merge now; phones carry the growing list until the follow-up ships.
I leave it, and tell azulus why. The list keeps growing with every delete.

The freeze lifts Monday. #129146 is the core change: it adds the actor to ViewerContext, and the eight per-team PRs read it. Each per-team PR could ship behind its own flag, so they don't strictly wait on the core one, but without it their flags do nothing.

Landing the core first is the safe order; landing a team's first would let that team test its flag earlier. Tell me the order you want.

now.author: me
now.why: handed back: the keep-alive test times out on Node 22 only; it needs a decision on the default

preflight.summary: Accepts cleartext HTTP/2 when a client opens with the h2 preface, behind a new http2: 'prior-knowledge' option. HTTP/1.1 on the same port keeps working.
concerns: The preface sniff waits for 24 bytes, so an HTTP/1 client that sends less sits out the 5 s sniff timeout.

now.title: Retry dead-lettered jobs with jittered backoff
now.author: marco

preflight.summary: Retries dead-lettered jobs up to 5 times with full-jitter backoff capped at 10 minutes, and keeps the attempt count in a column so it survives a worker restart.
concerns: Webhook jobs aren't idempotent: one that timed out after the request went out will deliver twice.

now.title: Stream partial results from the query planner
now.author: priya

preflight.summary: Adds a streaming scan (`streamRows`) and uses it in `runPlan`, so a query that runs past its time budget returns the rows found so far, marked partial. The `/v2/query` route passes an optional `?budget=` through and sets `X-Partial-Results`.
concerns: src/routes/query.ts passes ?budget= through Number() unchecked: a non-numeric value becomes NaN and silently turns the budget off, and 0 or a negative value returns an empty partial result.
Every query now has a 2 s budget by default, so slow queries that used to complete will come back partial; clients that ignore the new partial flag will treat them as complete.

now.title: Drop the legacy v1 auth middleware
now.author: dana

preflight.summary: Removes the v1 session-cookie middleware and moves the four routes that still used it onto token auth. Most of the diff deletes compatibility shims and their tests.
preflight.since: Moves `/v1/export` onto token auth too and adds a `Deprecation` header, but cookie callers still break with no window to switch.
concerns: `/v1/export` still sees session-cookie traffic; dropping it here breaks those callers with no deprecation window.

now.title: Add idempotency keys to webhook delivery
now.author: me

now.title: Capture unhandled rejections in edge runtimes
now.author: dana

preflight.summary: Listens for `unhandledrejection` in edge runtimes and reports `event.reason` as an unhandled error, so a promise that rejects with no catch shows up in Sentry. The handler lives in `edgeRejectionIntegration()` and is added only when `globalThis.EdgeRuntime` is set; Node keeps its own `onUnhandledRejection` integration. A reason that isn't an `Error` (a string, say) is wrapped in a synthetic one, so it still gets a stack. The new `captureUnhandledRejections` option defaults to on. Tests cover an `Error` reason, a string reason and the Node path, as https://github.com/nadia/sentry-javascript-integrations/issues/14390 asked.

today.title: Rewrite the tokenizer with a state table
today.author: wren

preflight.summary: Replaces the hand-written tokenizer with a generated state table and a short driver loop. Token positions now count UTF-16 code units instead of bytes.
concerns: Offsets after any non-ASCII character shift; tools that slice the source by byte offset will break without an error.
The 1,400-line table is checked in, but CI never regenerates it, so a grammar edit without rerunning the script ships a stale table.

today.title: Split the scheduler into lease and dispatch
today.author: kofi
today.why: your team's scheduler, and kofi waits on you

preflight.summary: Splits the scheduler in two. Lease owns the jobs table: it hands out time-limited leases with a fencing token, renews them on heartbeat and reclaims expired ones every 15 s. Dispatch asks Lease for work, runs it and reports back with the token, so a worker that lost its lease can't overwrite a newer result. The old scheduler stays behind SCHEDULER_V2=false for a release and reads the same table, so a rollback needs no migration. Most of the 1,240 lines move existing code; about 300 are new, mainly the renewal loop and its tests.
concerns: Both services run migrations on start, so two replicas starting together can race on the new lease_token column.
